summary_paragraph: A woman with primary sclerosing cholangitis, cirrhosis, and a history of recurrent cholangitis was admitted for right upper quadrant abdominal pain, low-grade fever, and malaise. She had completed a course of meropenem for a prior cholangitis episode two weeks earlier. Initial concern was for recurrent cholangitis, so she was started on meropenem again. Imaging showed no bile duct dilation, abscess, or dominant stricture, and cultures were negative. The infectious disease team concluded this was not acute cholangitis but recommended completing a short course of antibiotics given her history. Her symptoms resolved, liver enzymes improved, and she remained afebrile. Diuretics were held initially but resumed at discharge. She was discharged home with plans to complete IV antibiotics via her PICC line, continue all home medications, and follow up for liver clinic visits and a colonoscopy. Her transplant status remains unchanged.
